title: Custom Robo
subtitle: Build a small robot for the next contest
summary: Custom Robo is Noise and Studiofake's action role-playing game, first released for GameCube in Japan on 4 March 2004.
body: Custom Robo is Noise and Studiofake's action role-playing game, first released for GameCube in Japan on 4 March 2004. Known there as Custom Robo: Battle Revolution, it became the series' first release outside Japan. Human commanders enter battles through miniature robots, assembling a machine from interchangeable parts before fighting in a virtual Holosseum. A story campaign follows a new commander's encounters and investigations, giving each battle a place in a larger journey while new equipment expands the possibilities for the next match.

The robot consists of a body, gun, bomb, pod and leg parts. Changing them affects movement and the kinds of attacks available, allowing the player to build around a preferred range or tactic. Holosseums vary in shape and can contain hazards such as ice or lava. A configuration that worked in one arena may have difficulty maintaining distance in another. Preparation and direct control therefore remain connected: choosing the equipment establishes the tools, but movement and timing determine whether those tools suit the encounter.

Outside the arena, the player moves through the human world and speaks to characters who advance the campaign. Inside it, the focus narrows to the selected robot and its opponent. Completing A New Journey opens The Grand Battle, a sequence of tournaments that gives the assembled collection another use. Takayuki Nakamura composed the score. The shift between those scales makes customisation personal: the small machine entering the next Holosseum is the result of decisions made throughout the commander's progress.
